display.purpose: The one page heading. Course purple capitals, with the key word in map black.

title.purpose: Item headings inside a section, in capitals. Always map black.

lead.purpose: The paragraph directly under a heading.

body.purpose: All other reading text. Tabular figures.

caption.purpose: The map note, key entries and the copyright line.

label.purpose: Map lettering in spaced capitals: nav links, row labels, the sheet caption, badges.

motion.name: ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: The one easing curve. Used for every transition and for the course drawing.

motion.name: state-swap
motion.purpose: Button ink and ground swap, and nav link colour change.

motion.name: course-leg
motion.purpose: Each course leg is drawn along its length, once, on load.

motion.name: course-mark
motion.purpose: Each control ring and number appears, scaling from 1.5 to 1.

motion.name: course-tag
motion.purpose: Each tag slides in 10px from the left, 130ms after its control.

motion.name: course-step
motion.purpose: Delay between one course step and the next. The first step starts at 250ms.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: With reduced motion set, every animation and transition is cut to nothing and smooth scrolling is off.

narrative.overview:
Margincite is drawn as an orienteering map. The website is the terrain. The fixes are a course across it: a start triangle, numbered control rings, and straight purple legs between them. The rest of the page is treated as parts of the same printed sheet: a title block, a margin strip that holds the key, ruled legend tables, a control description sheet, and a north arrow and scale bar at the foot.

The sheet is white. A small set of flat spot inks is printed on it, and each ink has one job. Headings are tall condensed gothic capitals. Reading text is a plain semi-condensed sans. Rules are solid and 2px wide. Corners are 4px. Nothing has depth. Things sit on top of each other in print order, and lettering that crosses line work gets a white knock-out behind it.

The look refuses the usual SaaS landing page of gradient hero, product screenshot and three feature cards. It has to be memorable without being playful, because the product asks to be trusted with evidence.

The same look is planned for the Electron desktop app. That work is not built. Dense tables in the app will need a plain readable face for data. The display capitals are for headings and control numbers only. See the note under Typography.
keyCharacteristics: White sheet, flat spot inks, no gradients and no shadows.
Course purple carries the course, the main rules, the buttons and the main headings.
Tall condensed gothic capitals for headings. Plain semi-condensed sans for everything read.
Solid 2px rules divide the sheet. Corners are 4px.
Open control rings, a start triangle and a double-ring finish mark the order of things.
Buttons have one active state: ink and ground swap.
Every illustrated map or report is labelled as an example.

rules.name: The Spot Ink Rule
rules.body: Every fill is one flat, solid ink. No gradients. No drop shadows. No translucent fills. No blend modes, including on the course where it crosses terrain.

rules.name: The Course Purple Rule
rules.body: The course is always plain Course Purple. Legs, rings, the start triangle and control numbers are never tinted, never made translucent, and never drawn in another ink on a map. On the purple field the course symbols swap to white, which is the same inversion buttons use.

rules.name: The Screened Line Rule
rules.body: Line work may be printed at reduced strength. The build does this in three places: the contour ground behind a section (16 to 30 percent), the magnetic north lines (60 percent) and the trails (80 percent). This applies to thin lines only. It is never a way to lighten a fill, a button, a border or lettering.

rules.name: The Map Ink Rule
rules.body: Green and blue stay on the map and in key swatches. Do not use them as section grounds, button colours or status colours.

rules.name: The No Stretch Rule
rules.body: Lettering is never stretched, squeezed or scaled on one axis to fit a box. The box is sized to the lettering. Map tags measure their text and size the box from it. The map itself crops to fill its frame and is never distorted.

rules.name: The Capitals Rule
rules.body: League Gothic is always capitals at weight 400. It is never faked bold, never set in lower case, and never used for running text.

rules.name: The Data Face Note (planned, not built)
rules.body: When this look moves to the desktop app, dense tables need a plain readable face for data. Do not set table data in League Gothic. Barlow Semi Condensed with tabular figures is the only reading face the build has. Whether it serves dense tables at small sizes, or a plainer face is added for data, has not been decided.

rules.name: The Flat Sheet Rule
rules.body: If something needs to stand out from what is behind it, give it a solid white ground and a solid rule. Never a shadow, a blur or a see-through panel.

rules.name: The Knock-Out Rule
rules.body: Lettering on the map never has line work running through it. Give it a white box behind, or a white outline around each letter.

rules.name: The Open Ring Rule
rules.body: A control is an open ring. It is never filled, so the ground under it stays visible. This holds on the map and wherever a control ring is used as a marker.

rules.name: The Short Leg Rule
rules.body: Course legs are straight and stop short of the marks at both ends.

rules.name: The Inversion Rule
rules.body: The only active state on a button is a strict swap of ink and ground. No lift, no shadow, no scale, no tint, no darker shade of the same colour.

rules.name: The Example Label Rule
rules.body: The hero map shows an imaginary site. It always carries the example badge and the note that it is an illustration and not a screenshot. Any other illustrated report or interface carries the badge too.

dos: Do print every fill as one flat ink from the palette.
Do keep the course plain Course Purple, with open control rings and straight legs that stop short of each mark.
Do make the hover state of every button a strict swap of ink and ground, with the border unchanged.
Do size boxes to their lettering. Measure the text, then draw the box.
Do label every illustrated map, report or interface with the example badge.
Do divide content with solid 2px rules and changes of ground.
Do put a white knock-out or a white halo behind any lettering that sits on the map.
Do use 4px corners on every box.
Do set League Gothic in capitals at weight 400 for headings and control numbers only.
Do keep the skip link, visible focus outlines and reduced-motion handling on every new surface.
Do use a plain readable face with tabular figures for data when this look moves to the desktop app.
donts: Don't use gradients, drop shadows, glows, blurs or translucent fills.
Don't put a blend mode on the course, or tint it, or draw it in another ink on a map.
Don't give a button any active state other than the ink and ground swap. No lift, no scale, no darker shade.
Don't stretch, squeeze or scale lettering on one axis to fit a box.
Don't show the hero map, or any illustrated report, without its example label.
Don't use green or blue outside a map or a key swatch.
Don't set running text or table data in League Gothic.
Don't build the SaaS hero of gradient, screenshot and three feature cards. Lists are ruled tables, not cards.
Don't edit the generated terrain files by hand. Change the script and regenerate.
Don't lighten a fill, a border or lettering with opacity. Reduced strength is for thin map line work only.
